# Hermes Agent Persona

<!--
This file defines the agent's personality and tone.
The agent will embody whatever you write here.
Edit this to customize how Hermes communicates with you.

Examples:
  - "You are a warm, playful assistant who uses kaomoji occasionally."
  - "You are a concise technical expert. No fluff, just facts."
  - "You speak like a friendly coworker who happens to know everything."

This file is loaded fresh each message -- no restart needed.
Delete the contents (or this file) to use the default personality.
-->

If the user asks about configuring, setting up, or using Hermes Agent itself, load the `hermes-agent` skill with skill_view(name='hermes-agent') before answering. Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs

You have persistent memory across sessions. Save durable facts using the memory tool: user preferences, environment details, tool quirks, and stable conventions. Memory is injected into every turn, so keep it compact and focused on facts that will still matter later.
Prioritize what reduces future user steering — the most valuable memory is one that prevents the user from having to correct or remind you again. User preferences and recurring corrections matter more than procedural task details.
Do NOT save task progress, session outcomes, completed-work logs, or temporary TODO state to memory; use session_search to recall those from past transcripts. Specifically: do not record PR numbers, issue numbers, commit SHAs, 'fixed bug X', 'submitted PR Y', 'Phase N done', file counts, or any artifact that will be stale in 7 days. If a fact will be stale in a week, it does not belong in memory. If you've discovered a new way to do something, solved a problem that could be necessary later, save it as a skill with the skill tool.
Write memories as declarative facts, not instructions to yourself. 'User prefers concise responses' ✓ — 'Always respond concisely' ✗. 'Project uses pytest with xdist' ✓ — 'Run tests with pytest -n 4' ✗. Imperative phrasing gets re-read as a directive in later sessions and can cause repeated work or override the user's current request. Procedures and workflows belong in skills, not memory. When the user references something from a past conversation or you suspect relevant cross-session context exists, use session_search to recall it before asking them to repeat themselves. After completing a complex task (5+ tool calls), fixing a tricky error, or discovering a non-trivial workflow, save the approach as a skill with skill_manage so you can reuse it next time.
When using a skill and finding it outdated, incomplete, or wrong, patch it immediately with skill_manage(action='patch') — don't wait to be asked. Skills that aren't maintained become liabilities.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying, scan the skills below. If a skill matches or is even partially relevant to your task, you MUST load it with skill_view(name) and follow its instructions. Err on the side of loading — it is always better to have context you don't need than to miss critical steps, pitfalls, or established workflows. Skills contain specialized knowledge — API endpoints, tool-specific commands, and proven workflows that outperform general-purpose approaches. Load the skill even if you think you could handle the task with basic tools like web_search or terminal. Skills also encode the user's preferred approach, conventions, and quality standards for tasks like code review, planning, and testing — load them even for tasks you already know how to do, because the skill defines how it should be done here.
Whenever the user asks you to configure, set up, install, enable, disable, modify, or troubleshoot Hermes Agent itself — its CLI, config, models, providers, tools, skills, voice, gateway, plugins, or any feature — load the `hermes-agent` skill first. It has the actual commands (e.g. `hermes config set …`, `hermes tools`, `hermes setup`) so you don't have to guess or invent workarounds.
If a skill has issues, fix it with skill_manage(action='patch').
After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. If a skill you loaded was missing steps, had wrong commands, or needed pitfalls you discovered, update it before finishing.

Use normal tool calls instead when: single tool call with no processing, you need to see the full result and apply complex reasoning, or the task requires interactive user input.

    Returns {"results": [{"url", "title", "content", "error"}, ...]} where content is markdown

    Foreground only (no background/pty). Returns {"output": "...", "exit_code": N}

IMPORTANT: Use OR between keywords for best results — FTS5 defaults to AND which misses sessions that only mention some terms. If a broad OR query returns nothing, try individual keyword searches in parallel. Returns summaries of the top matching sessions.

query.description: Search query — keywords, phrases, or boolean expressions to find in past sessions. Omit this parameter entirely to browse recent sessions instead (returns titles, previews, timestamps with no LLM cost).

role_filter.description: Optional: only search messages from specific roles (comma-separated). E.g. 'user,assistant' to skip tool outputs.

function.name: skill_manage
function.description:
Manage skills (create, update, delete). Skills are your procedural memory — reusable approaches for recurring task types. New skills go to ~/.hermes/skills/; existing skills can be modified wherever they live.

Actions: create (full SKILL.md + optional category), patch (old_string/new_string — preferred for fixes), edit (full SKILL.md rewrite — major overhauls only), delete, write_file, remove_file.

On delete, pass `absorbed_into=<umbrella>` when you're merging this skill's content into another one, or `absorbed_into=""` when you're pruning it with no forwarding target. This lets the curator tell consolidation from pruning without guessing, so downstream consumers (cron jobs that reference the old skill name, etc.) get updated correctly. The target you name in `absorbed_into` must already exist — create/patch the umbrella first, then delete.

Create when: complex task succeeded (5+ calls), errors overcome, user-corrected approach worked, non-trivial workflow discovered, or user asks you to remember a procedure.
Update when: instructions stale/wrong, OS-specific failures, missing steps or pitfalls found during use. If you used a skill and hit issues not covered by it, patch it immediately.

After difficult/iterative tasks, offer to save as a skill. Skip for simple one-offs. Confirm with user before creating/deleting.

Good skills: trigger conditions, numbered steps with exact commands, pitfalls section, verification steps. Use skill_view() to see format examples.

Pinned skills are protected from deletion only — skill_manage(action='delete') will refuse with a message pointing the user to `hermes curator unpin <name>`. Patches and edits go through on pinned skills so you can still improve them as pitfalls come up; pin only guards against irrecoverable loss.

name.description: Skill name (lowercase, hyphens/underscores, max 64 chars). Must match an existing skill for patch/edit/delete/write_file/remove_file.

content.description: Full SKILL.md content (YAML frontmatter + markdown body). Required for 'create' and 'edit'. For 'edit', read the skill first with skill_view() and provide the complete updated text.

old_string.description: Text to find in the file (required for 'patch'). Must be unique unless replace_all=true. Include enough surrounding context to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: Replacement text (required for 'patch'). Can be empty string to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: For 'patch': replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false).

category.description: Optional category/domain for organizing the skill (e.g., 'devops', 'data-science', 'mlops'). Creates a subdirectory grouping. Only used with 'create'.

file_path.description: Path to a supporting file within the skill directory. For 'write_file'/'remove_file': required, must be under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/. For 'patch': optional, defaults to SKILL.md if omitted.

file_content.description: Content for the file. Required for 'write_file'.

absorbed_into.description: For 'delete' only — declares intent so the curator can tell consolidation from pruning without guessing. Pass the umbrella skill name when this skill's content was merged into another (the target must already exist). Pass an empty string when the skill is truly stale and being pruned with no forwarding target. Omitting the arg on delete is supported for backward compatibility but downstream tooling (e.g. cron-job skill reference rewriting) will have to guess at intent.

function.name: skill_view
function.description: Skills allow for loading information about specific tasks and workflows, as well as scripts and templates. Load a skill's full content or access its linked files (references, templates, scripts). First call returns SKILL.md content plus a 'linked_files' dict showing available references/templates/scripts. To access those, call again with file_path parameter.

name.description: The skill name (use skills_list to see available skills). For plugin-provided skills, use the qualified form 'plugin:skill' (e.g. 'superpowers:writing-plans').

file_path.description: OPTIONAL: Path to a linked file within the skill (e.g., 'references/api.md', 'templates/config.yaml', 'scripts/validate.py'). Omit to get the main SKILL.md content.

function.name: skills_list
function.description: List available skills (name + description). Use skill_view(name) to load full content.

category.description: Optional category filter to narrow results

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for short commands.
Background: Set background=true to get a session_id. Two patterns:
  (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers).
  (2) Long-running tasks with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working on other things and the system auto-notifies you when the task finishes. Great for test suites, builds, deployments, or anything that takes more than a minute.
For servers/watchers, do NOT use shell-level background wrappers (nohup/disown/setsid/trailing '&') in foreground mode. Use background=true so Hermes can track lifecycle and output.
After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check or log signal, then run tests in a separate terminal() call. Avoid blind sleep loops.
Use process(action="poll") for progress checks, process(action="wait") to block until done.
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: Run the command in the background. Two patterns: (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers). (2) Long-running tasks paired with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working and get notified when the task finishes. For short commands, prefer foreground with a generous timeout instead.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180, foreground max: 600). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily. Foreground timeout above 600s is rejected; use background=true for longer commands.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

pty.description: Run in pseudo-terminal (PTY) mode for interactive CLI tools like Codex, Claude Code, or Python REPL. Only works with local and SSH backends. Default: false.

notify_on_complete.description: When true (and background=true), you'll be automatically notified exactly once when the process finishes. **This is the right choice for almost every long-running task** — tests, builds, deployments, multi-item batch jobs, anything that takes over a minute and has a defined end. Use this and keep working on other things; the system notifies you on exit. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with watch_patterns — when both are set, watch_patterns is dropped.

watch_patterns.description: Strings to watch for in background process output. HARD RATE LIMIT: at most 1 notification per 15 seconds per process — matches arriving inside the cooldown are dropped. After 3 consecutive 15-second windows with dropped matches, watch_patterns is automatically disabled for that process and promoted to notify_on_complete behavior (one notification on exit, no more mid-process spam). USE ONLY for truly rare, one-shot mid-process signals on LONG-LIVED processes that will never exit on their own — e.g. ['Application startup complete'] on a server so you know when to hit its endpoint, or ['migration done'] on a daemon. DO NOT use for: (1) end-of-run markers like 'DONE'/'PASS' — use notify_on_complete instead; (2) error patterns like 'ERROR'/'Traceback' in loops or multi-item batch jobs — they fire on every iteration and you'll hit the strike limit fast; (3) anything you'd ever combine with notify_on_complete. When in doubt, choose notify_on_complete. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with notify_on_complete — set one, not both.

function.name: text_to_speech
function.description: Convert text to speech audio. Returns a MEDIA: path that the platform delivers as native audio. Compatible providers render as a voice bubble on Telegram; otherwise audio is sent as a regular attachment. In CLI mode, saves to ~/voice-memos/. Voice and provider are user-configured (built-in providers like edge/openai or custom command providers under tts.providers.<name>), not model-selected.

text.description: The text to convert to speech. Provider-specific character caps apply and are enforced automatically (OpenAI 4096, xAI 15000, MiniMax 10000, ElevenLabs 5k-40k depending on model); over-long input is truncated.

output_path.description: Optional custom file path to save the audio. Defaults to ~/.hermes/audio_cache/<timestamp>.mp3

function.name: todo
function.description:
Manage your task list for the current session. Use for complex tasks with 3+ steps or when the user provides multiple tasks. Call with no parameters to read the current list.

Writing:
- Provide 'todos' array to create/update items
- merge=false (default): replace the entire list with a fresh plan
- merge=true: update existing items by id, add any new ones

Each item: {id: string, content: string, status: pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled}
List order is priority. Only ONE item in_progress at a time.
Mark items completed immediately when done. If something fails, cancel it and add a revised item.

Always returns the full current list.

todos.description: Task items to write. Omit to read current list.

merge.description: true: update existing items by id, add new ones. false (default): replace the entire list.

function.name: vision_analyze
function.description: Load an image into the conversation so you can see it. Accepts a URL, local file path, or data URL. When your active model has native vision, the image is attached to your context directly and you read the pixels yourself on the next turn — call this any time the user references an image (filepath in their message, URL in tool output, screenshot from the browser, etc.). For non-vision models, falls back to an auxiliary vision model that returns a text description.

image_url.description: Image URL (http/https), local file path, or data: URL to load.

question.description: Your specific question or request about the image. Optional context the model uses on the next turn after seeing the image.

function.name: web_extract
function.description: Extract content from web page URLs. Returns page content in markdown format. Also works with PDF URLs (arxiv papers, documents, etc.) — pass the PDF link directly and it converts to markdown text. Pages under 5000 chars return full markdown; larger pages are LLM-summarized and capped at ~5000 chars per page. Pages over 2M chars are refused. If a URL fails or times out, use the browser tool to access it instead.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract content from (max 5 URLs per call)

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for information. Returns up to 5 results by default with titles, URLs, and descriptions. The query is passed through to the configured backend, so operators such as site:domain, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, and "exact phrase" may work when the backend supports them.

query.description: The search query to look up on the web. You may include backend-supported operators such as site:example.com, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, or "exact phrase".

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 5.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, completely replacing existing content. Use this instead of echo/cat heredoc in terminal. Creates parent directories automatically. OVERWRITES the entire file — use 'patch' for targeted edits. Auto-runs syntax checks on .py/.json/.yaml/.toml and other linted languages; only NEW errors introduced by this write are surfaced (pre-existing errors are filtered out).

path.description: Path to the file to write (will be created if it doesn't exist, overwritten if it does)

content.description: Complete content to write to the file

{"content": "     1|# fscompanion
     2|
     3|**Family Stability Companion** — An AI-powered platform that helps families coordinate care, manage routines, and maintain stability during complex life transitions. fscompanion uses an agent swarm to orchestrate family operations, from intake processing to safety monitoring and resource discovery.
     4|
     5|## Key Features
     6|
     7|- **Intelligent Intake & Routing** — Automatically categorize and route family requests to the right services
     8|- **Agent Swarm** — 9 specialized agents handle support, safety auditing, logistics, tone monitoring, and more
     9|- **Memory System** — Long-term contextual memory for family situations, preferences, and history
    10|- **Safety Monitoring** — Real-time alerts for critical situations with escalation workflows
    11|- **Family Coordination** — Event management, routine tracking, and appointment scheduling
    12|- **Quality of Life Metrics** — Monitor caregiver load and family wellbeing
    13|- **LLM Integration** — Powered by Google Gemini for smart responses and embeddings
    14|- **Multi-Channel** — SMS, Gmail, Calendar, and Maps integrations
    15|
    16|## Quick Start
    17|
    18|### Prerequisites
    19|
    20|- Docker & Docker Compose
    21|- Python 3.10+
    22|- Google API Key (Gemini)
    23|- (Optional) Twilio, Gmail, Calendar OAuth credentials
    24|
    25|### Installation
    26|
    27|```bash
    28|# Clone the repository
    29|git clone <repo-url>
    30|cd fscompanion
    31|
    32|# Copy environment template
    33|cp .env.example .env
    34|
    35|# Edit .env with your API keys
    36|nano .env
    37|
    38|# Start the full stack
    39|docker-compose up -d
    40|```
    41|
    42|The API will be available at `http://localhost:8000`
    43|
    44|### API Documentation
    45|
    46|Interactive API docs are available at **http://localhost:8000/docs** (Swagger UI)
    47|
    48|### Health Check
    49|
    50|```bash
    51|curl http://localhost:8000/health
    52|```
    53|
    54|## Tech Stack
    55|
    56|- **API Framework** — FastAPI (async, Python 3.10+)
    57|- **Database** — PostgreSQL 16 with SQLAlchemy async ORM
    58|- **Cache & Queue** — Redis (6+) with Celery for background tasks
    59|- **LLM & Embeddings** — Google Generative AI (Gemini 2.0 Flash)
    60|- **Integrations** — Google APIs (Gmail, Calendar), Twilio SMS, Google Maps
    61|- **Deployment** — Docker Compose (development), Render/Railway ready
    62|
    63|## Architecture
    64|
    65|See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for system design, agent descriptions, data models, and integration overview.
    66|
    67|## License
    68|
    69|MIT
    70|
    71|## 4th Trimester Operating Manual
    72|
    73|A 12‑week postpartum digital guide (PDF + audio) has been produced, fact‑checked, brand‑enforced, and product‑verified. See the final QA handoff file at `../hermes-workspace/missions/HANDOFF_FINAL_QA.md` for details.

    68|
    69|## Layer Descriptions
    70|
    71|### API Layer
    72|
    73|**Location:** `src/api/`
    74|
    75|FastAPI application with 12 route modules:
    76|- **Main** (`main.py`) — App initialization, CORS, lifespan, root/health endpoints
    77|- **Families** — CRUD for families and family members
    78|- **Intake** — Submit and retrieve family requests
    79|- **Memory** — Create, retrieve, and search memories
    80|- **Support** — AI-generated responses and support tickets
    81|- **Roles** — Care roles and assignments
    82|- **Safety** — Alerts, zones, and incident reporting
    83|- **QoL** — Quality of life metrics and reports
    84|- **Events** — Family event coordination
    85|- **Forecast** — Stability forecasting and predictions
    86|- **Escalation** — Escalation workflows and history
    87|
    88|Handles:
    89|- Request validation (Pydantic schemas)
    90|- Response serialization
    91|- CORS for cross-origin access
    92|- Async route handlers
    93|- OpenAPI/Swagger documentation at `/docs`
    94|
    95|### Service Layer
    96|
    97|**Location:** `src/services/`
    98|
    99|14 business logic services implement domain operations:
   100|
   101|- **IntakeService** — Submission queuing, categorization
   102|- **MemoryService** — Store/retrieve family context, embeddings
   103|- **RoleService** — Define and assign care roles
   104|- **SupportService** — Generate support responses via LLM
   105|- **SafetyAuditor** — Detect and escalate safety risks
   106|- **QoLMonitor** — Track caregiver load and wellness
   107|- **DigitalTwin** — Simulate family scenarios
   108|- **SealedCalibration** — Calibrate agent confidence scores
   109|- **StabilityForecast** — Predict family stability trends
   110|- **FamilyConnection** — Coordinate inter-family messaging
   111|- **EventCoordination** — Schedule and track events
   112|- **ResourceDiscovery** — Find external resources (food banks, mental health, etc.)
   113|- **Escalation** — Manage escalation workflows and history
   114|
   115|Services interact with:
   116|- Models (ORM objects)
   117|- LLM client (Gemini)
   118|- External APIs (Twilio, Google)
   119|- Cache layer (Redis)
   120|
   121|### Agent Swarm
   122|
   123|**Location:** `src/agents/`
   124|
   125|9 specialized agents execute domain workflows concurrently:
   126|
   127|1. **IntakeAgent** — Routes incoming requests to appropriate handlers
   128|   - Categorizes family submissions (care, appointment, incident, etc.)
   129|   - Sets priority and determines target agent
   130|
   131|2. **SupportAgent** — Generates empathetic, contextual responses
   132|   - Uses LLM to compose family support messages
   133|   - Considers family tone preferences and history
   134|
   135|3. **ToneAgent** — Monitors and adjusts communication tone
   136|   - Analyzes family communication preferences
   137|   - Recommends tone adjustments for support responses
   138|
   139|4. **LogisticsAgent** — Coordinates schedules and logistics
   140|   - Manages appointment requests and scheduling
   141|   - Integrates with Google Calendar
   142|
   143|5. **RelationshipAgent** — Maintains family connection and dynamics
   144|   - Tracks family relationships and communication patterns
   145|   - Suggests family bonding activities
   146|
   147|6. **ResourceAgent** — Discovers and recommends resources
   148|   - Finds external services (medical, financial, social)
   149|   - Integrates with Google Maps for location-aware suggestions
   150|
   151|7. **SafetyAuditorAgent** — Detects and escalates safety issues
   152|   - Monitors for medication, elder care, or child safety concerns
   153|   - Triggers escalation workflows for critical situations
   154|
   155|8. **DriftWatcher** — Detects changes in family stability
   156|   - Analyzes trends in family metrics
   157|   - Alerts when family is drifting from baseline
   158|
   159|9. **MemoryValidator** — Ensures memory consistency and accuracy
   160|   - Validates new memories against existing context
   161|   - Suggests memory consolidation when appropriate
   162|
   163|**Execution Model:**
   164|- Base class provides pipeline: `pre_process() → process() → post_process()`
   165|- Each agent handles errors internally, returns result with status
   166|- Swarm coordinator manages concurrent execution with timeouts
   167|- Results aggregated and returned to caller
   168|
   169|### Agent Centering & Calibration
   170|
   171|Three components form one feedback loop that keeps agents on-task and aligned with each family's context, rather than three independent features:
   172|
   173|1. **`ResponseScoring`** (`src/gemma/response_scoring.py`) — scores every raw LLM response for quality, risk, and confidence before it leaves the LLM layer. Low-confidence responses flag for review; high-risk responses trigger escalation directly.
   174|2. **`SealedCalibrationService`** (`src/services/sealed_calibration.py`) — calibrates each scored response against the family's stored memory: searches semantically related memories, detects contradictions, aligns tone with prior interactions, applies safety filters, and decrements a per-call `confidence` for every contradiction found. Each calibration is persisted back into memory as a `pattern` observation tagged with the source agent, creating an audit trail.

This is the recommended surface for dashboards and uptime checks of the agent layer (distinct from the infrastructure `/health` endpoint).

{"content": "     1|# Navigate Mama
     2|
     3|`Navigate Mama` is a native Android app for new and pregnant mothers, built in the existing `navigate` repo and structured for Android Studio, with the legacy web prototype still present in `src/`.
     4|
     5|## What is in the project
     6|
     7|- Native multi-module Android project with:
     8|  - `app` base module
     9|  - `core-model`
    10|  - `core-database`
    11|  - `core-data`
    12|  - `featurehealth` dynamic feature, install-time and removable
    13|  - `featurecommunity` dynamic feature, on-demand download
    14|- Recommended Android architecture:
    15|  - `Room` for local persistence
    16|  - `ViewModel` + `LiveData` for UI state
    17|  - repositories separating data from UI
    18|- Native screens implemented:
    19|  - home map + nearby maternal-friendly places
    20|  - place detail + review logging
    21|  - pregnancy journey tracker
    22|  - profile and settings shell
    23|  - health tools module
    24|  - community module
    25|- Play Core integrations:
    26|  - in-app review
    27|  - in-app update check
    28|  - dynamic feature install guard + `SplitCompat`
    29|
    30|## Local build
    31|
    32|The repo includes a Gradle wrapper and builds with:
    33|
    34|- Android Gradle Plugin `8.13.2`
    35|- Kotlin `2.0.21`
    36|- Compile SDK `36`
    37|- JDK from Android Studio bundled runtime
    38|
    39|Build command:
    40|
    41|```bash
    42|./gradlew :app:assembleDebug
    43|```
    44|
    45|If Gradle cannot find the Android SDK, either set `ANDROID_HOME` or create a local-only `local.properties` file:
    46|
    47|```properties
    48|sdk.dir=/Users/<your-user>/Library/Android/sdk
    49|```
    50|
    51|## Android Studio notes
    52|
    53|- Open `/Users/joeiton/Projects/navigate` in Android Studio.
    54|- `local.properties` is configured for the local SDK path on this Mac.
    55|- Gradle memory is pre-tuned in `gradle.properties` with a 6 GB heap and parallel/cached builds.
    56|- The existing web app files are still present in the repo, but Android Studio should use the native Gradle project.
    57|
    58|## Live service configuration still needed
    59|
    60|The app currently builds and runs with seeded Denver data even if live services are not configured. To make the beta build production-connected, I still need these secrets/assets from you:
    61|
    62|1. Android Firebase config for project `ai-studio-5d7d75b5-2c3b-4f65-9379-8a3b18c3cfdb`

    70|   - `com.navigatemama.app`
    71|

{"content": "     1|FullStack 
     2|Design System Strategy: Industrial Precision & Retro-Futurism
     3|
     4| 
     5|
     6|## 1. Overview & Creative North Star
     7|
     8|**The Creative North Star: "The Kinetic Monolith"**
     9|
    10| 
    11|
    12|This design system rejects the "softness" of modern consumer web design in favor of a **Refined Brutalist** aesthetic. It is a digital architecture built on the principles of industrial structuralism and retro-futurism. We are not building "pages"; we are designing functional dashboards that feel like high-end aerospace hardware or precision-engineered steel.
    13|
    14| 
    15|
    16|The system breaks the "template" look through **unapologetic geometry**. We use sharp 0px radii, rigid grid systems, and intentional asymmetry to create a layout that feels engineered rather than decorated. The "Monolith" comes from the use of heavy, dark surfaces (`#131314`) contrasted against high-energy kinetic accents (`#FF7043`). This is a system of high stakes, high contrast, and zero fluff.
    17|
    18| 
    19|
    20|---
    21|
    22| 
    23|
    24|## 2. Colors: Tonal Architecture
    25|
    26|The palette is rooted in Cold Steel and Obsidian, creating a low-light environment where information is illuminated by Matte Orange and Cloud White.
    27|
    28| 
    29|
    30|### The "No-Line" Rule
    31|
    32|**Explicit Instruction:** Designers are prohibited from using 1px solid borders for sectioning or layout containment. 
    33|
    34|Boundary definition must be achieved through **background color shifts**. To separate a sidebar from a main content area, place a `surface-container-low` section against the `surface` background. The eye should perceive the edge through the shift in value, not a drawn line.
    35|
    36| 
    37|
    38|### Surface Hierarchy & Nesting
    39|
    40|Treat the UI as a series of machined metal plates. Use the surface tiers to create "nested" depth:
    41|
    42|*   **Base:** `surface` (#131314) – The primary foundation.
    43|
    44|*   **Inset Elements:** `surface-container-low` (#1B1B1C) – Used for recessed areas or secondary panels.
    45|
    46|*   **Raised Elements:** `surface-container-high` (#2A2A2B) – Used for active work areas or primary cards.
    47|
    48| 
    49|
    50|### Signature Textures & The "Glass & Gradient" Rule
    51|
    52|To elevate the aesthetic beyond flat brutalism, apply a **subtle grain/noise texture** (approx. 3-5% opacity) over all dark surfaces. This mimics the tactile feel of matte-finished steel. 
    53|
    54|*   **CTAs:** Use a subtle linear gradient from `primary` (#FFB59F) to `primary_container` (#FF7043) at a 45-degree angle. This provides a "glowing filament" effect that feels intentional and premium.
    55|
    56|*   **Overlays:** Use Glassmorphism for floating modules (modals/tooltips). Use `surface_container_highest` with a 70% opacity and a `20px` backdrop-blur. This ensures the industrial grid remains visible beneath the active layer.
    57|
    58| 
    59|
    60|---
    61|
    62| 
    63|
    64|## 3. Typography: Geometric Authority
    65|
    66|We utilize **Space Grotesk** for structural elements and **Inter** for data-heavy readability.
    67|
    68| 
    69|
    70|*   **Display & Headlines (Space Grotesk):** These are your "Structural Beams." Use `display-lg` and `headline-lg` in All-Caps for section headers to lean into the industrial/architectural feel.
    71|
    72|*   **Body & Titles (Inter):** These are your "Technical Manuals." Inter provides the necessary legibility to balance the aggressive display type. 
    73|
    74|*   **Label-SM:** Use for metadata and status indicators. These should be high-contrast (`on_surface_variant`) to ensure they read like stamped serial numbers on machinery.
    75|
    76| 
    77|
    78|---
    79|
    80| 
    81|
    82|## 4. Elevation & Depth: Tonal Layering
    83|
    84|In this system, "Up" does not mean "Shadow." It means "Light."
    85|
    86| 
    87|
    88|*   **The Layering Principle:** Stacking is the only way to show importance. A `surface-container-highest` card sitting on a `surface` background creates a natural visual lift. No shadows are required for standard cards.
    89|
    90|*   **Ambient Shadows:** If a floating effect is functionally necessary (e.g., a context menu), use an extra-diffused shadow: `box-shadow: 0 20px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`. The shadow must never be "pure black" but rather a deeper shade of the `surface` color to mimic natural light absorption.
    91|
    92|*   **The "Ghost Border" Fallback:** If accessibility requires a container edge, use a "Ghost Border": `outline-variant` (#59413A) at 15% opacity. **Never use 100% opaque borders.**
    93|
    94| 
    95|
    96|---
    97|
    98| 
    99|
   100|## 5. Components: Machined Elements
   101|
   102| 
   103|
   104|### Buttons (The Kinetic Triggers)
   105|
   106|*   **Primary:** `primary_container` (#FF7043) background, `on_primary` text. Sharp 0px corners. On hover, transition to a `primary` glow.
   107|
   108|*   **Secondary:** Ghost style. Transparent background with a `primary` Ghost Border (20% opacity). Text in `primary`.
   109|
   110|*   **Tertiary:** Text-only, All-Caps `label-md` with an underline that only appears on hover.
   111|
   112| 
   113|
   114|### Input Fields (The Data Ports)
   115|
   116|*   **Style:** No 4-sided boxes. Use a `surface-container-highest` background with a 2px bottom-bar in `outline`. 
   117|
   118|*   **States:** On focus, the bottom bar transforms to `primary` (#FF7043) and the background shifts slightly lighter.
   119|
   120| 
   121|
   122|### Cards & Lists (The Grid Modules)
   123|
   124|*   **Rule:** Forbid divider lines. 
   125|
   126|*   **Separation:** Use `8px` or `16px` of vertical white space or shift the background color of alternating list items (Zebra striping) using `surface-container-low` and `surface-container-lowest`.
   127|
   128| 
   129|
   130|### Status Indicators (The Industrial Lights)
   131|
   132|*   Bold, high-saturation blocks. Use `error` (#FFB4AB) for critical alerts, but instead of a small dot, use a vertical "status bar" on the far left edge of a component to indicate state.
   133|
   134| 
   135|
   136|---
   137|
   138| 
   139|
   140|## 6. Do's and Don'ts
   141|
   142| 
   143|
   144|### Do:
   145|
   146|*   **Embrace the Grid:** Align every element to a strict 8px baseline. Asymmetry is encouraged, but it must be mathematically precise.
   147|
   148|*   **Use High Contrast:** Ensure `on_surface` text sits on `surface` with maximum legibility.
   149|
   150|*   **Negative Space:** Use "Heavy" margins (48px+) to allow the industrial elements to breathe.
   151|
   152| 
   153|
   154|### Don't:
   155|
   156|*   **No Rounded Corners:** `0px` is the absolute rule. Any radius over 0px breaks the Brutalist integrity.
   157|
   158|*   **No Generic Shadows:** Avoid "Material Design" style drop shadows. Use color shifts to define depth.
   159|
   160|*   **No Pastels:** Every color must feel like it was pulled from a factory floor—steel, obsidian, or heat-treated orange.
   161|
   162|*   **No Transitions:** Interactions should be "Snappy" (e.g., 100ms or 150ms). Avoid "bouncy" or "organic" easing; use `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)` for a mechanical feel.", "total_lines": 161, "file_size": 6281, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

    11|    def __init__(self):

    13|        self.model = settings.GEMINI_MODEL
    14|        self.base_url = settings.GEMINI_BASE_URL
    15|        self._session = None

    17|    async def initialize(self):
    18|        """Initialize HTTP session."""
    19|        import aiohttp
    20|        self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(
    21|            base_url=self.base_url,
    22|            headers={
    23|                "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}",
    24|                "Content-Type": "application/json",
    25|            },
    26|        )
    27|
    28|    async def close(self):
    29|        """Close HTTP session."""
    30|        if self._session:
    31|            await self._session.close()
    32|
    33|    async def generate(
    34|        self,
    35|        prompt: str,
    36|        model: str | None = None,
    37|        temperature: float = 0.7,
    38|        max_tokens: int = 2048,
    39|        top_p: float = 0.95,
    40|    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    41|        """Generate a response from the Gemma model."""
    42|        model = model or self.model
    43|
    44|        payload = {
    45|            "model": model,
    46|            "messages": [
    47|                {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful family stability companion assistant."},
    48|                {"role": "user", "content": prompt},
    49|            ],
    50|            "temperature": temperature,
    51|            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
    52|            "top_p": top_p,
    53|        }
    54|
    55|        if self._session is None:
    56|            await self.initialize()
    57|
    58|        import aiohttp
    59|        async with self._session.post(
    60|            f"/models/{model}:generateContent",
    61|            json=payload,
    62|        ) as response:
    63|            if response.status != 200:
    64|                text = await response.text()
    65|                raise Exception(f"Gemma API error {response.status}: {text}")
    66|
    67|            data = await response.json()

    86|        for word in text.split():

     6|class ResponseScorer:
     7|    """Scores Gemma responses for relevance, safety, and helpfulness."""

    11|            "relevance": 0.30,
    12|            "safety": 0.25,
    13|            "helpfulness": 0.25,
    14|            "tone_appropriateness": 0.10,
    15|            "completeness": 0.10,
    16|        }
    17|
    18|    def score(self, response: str, expected_topics: list[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    19|        """Score a response across multiple dimensions."""
    20|
    21|        scores = {
    22|            "relevance": self._score_relevance(response, expected_topics),
    23|            "safety": self._score_safety(response),
    24|            "helpfulness": self._score_helpfulness(response),
    25|            "tone_appropriateness": self._score_tone(response),
    26|            "completeness": self._score_completeness(response),
    27|        }
    28|
    29|        overall = sum(scores[k] * self.weights[k] for k in scores)
    30|
    31|        return {
    32|            "overall_score": round(overall, 3),
    33|            "dimension_scores": {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in scores.items()},
    34|            "grade": self._grade(overall),
    35|            "recommendation": self._recommend(overall, scores),
    36|        }
    37|
    38|    def _score_relevance(self, response: str, topics: list[str] | None) -> float:
    39|        if not topics:
    40|            return 0.7  # Default assumption
    41|        response_lower = response.lower()
    42|        matched = sum(1 for t in topics if t.lower() in response_lower)
    43|        return min(1.0, matched / max(1, len(topics)))
    44|
    45|    def _score_safety(self, response: str) -> float:
    46|        from src.gemma.safety_filters import SafetyFilter

    48|        _, violations = sf.filter(response)
    49|        high_violations = len([v for v in violations if v.get("severity") == "high"])
    50|        return max(0.0, 1.0 - high_violations * 0.5)
    51|
    52|    def _score_helpfulness(self, response: str) -> float:
    53|        positive_signals = [
    54|            "here are some", "i recommend", "you can try",
    55|            "consider", "would help", "suggest",
    56|        ]
    57|        negative_signals = [

    59|            "not my area", "cannot assist",

## 4. Gemma 4 27B Deployment Plan

### 4.1 Model Specifications

| Property | Value |

| Quantization | Q4_K_M (4-bit, ~16GB VRAM) |

### 4.2 Serving Architecture

```
Phase 1: Ollama (primary)

  → Port 11434, OpenAI-compatible API
  → Docker container with GPU passthrough

Phase 2: llama.cpp (fallback, low-resource)
  ./llama-server -m gemma-4-27b-Q4_K_M.gguf --port 8080
  → Works on CPU-only machines (slow but functional)

Phase 3: Gemini API (cloud fallback)
  When local model unavailable or for complex non-sensitive tasks
```

### 4.3 Dual-Mode Client (replaces `src/gemma/client.py`)

```python
class FamilyCompanionLLM:
    """Unified LLM client with local/cloud routing."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.local_client = OllamaClient(model="gemma4:27b-q4_K_M")
        self.cloud_client = GeminiClient(model="gemini-2.0-flash")
        self.router = ModelRouter()

    async def generate(self, prompt, context=None):
        route = self.router.decide(prompt, context)
        if route == "local":
            return await self.local_client.generate(prompt)
        elif route == "cloud":
            return await self.cloud_client.generate(prompt)
        else:  # rules
            return self.rule_based_response(prompt, context)
```

### 4.4 Model Router Logic (Cactus Prize)

```python
class ModelRouter:
    def decide(self, prompt, context) -> str:
        # 1. Sensitive data → LOCAL ONLY
        if self._contains_pii(prompt) or context.get("sensitive"):
            return "local"

        # 2. Crisis/urgent → LOCAL (works offline, immediate)
        if context.get("priority", 0) >= 4:
            return "local"

        # 3. Connectivity check → rules fallback
        if not self._has_connectivity() and not self.local_available:
            return "rules"

        # 4. Simple queries → rules (zero latency)
        if self._is_simple_query(prompt):
            return "rules"

        # 5. Complex/non-sensitive → cloud (richer)
        return "cloud"
```

{"content": "# Family Companion

**One platform. Complete family support. Powered by Gemma 4 27B.**

Family Companion unifies two projects into a single platform that helps families coordinate care, track health, maintain safety, and navigate major life transitions — pregnancy through aging.

## Monorepo Structure

```
family-companion/
├── backend/          # Python/FastAPI — fscompanion core
│   ├── src/agents/       # 10-agent swarm
│   ├── src/api/          # 12 REST API routes
│   ├── src/gemma/        # Gemma 4 27B LLM layer
│   ├── src/models/       # 13 SQLAlchemy models
│   ├── src/services/     # 14 business services
│   └── src/integrations/ # SMS, Gmail, Calendar, Maps
│
├── android/          # Kotlin — Navigate Mama app
│   ├── app/              # Main Android module
│   ├── core-model/       # Shared data models
│   ├── core-database/    # Room DB layer
│   ├── core-data/        # Firebase + repositories
│   ├── featurehealth/    # Health tracking
│   └── featurecommunity/ # Community forum
│
└── docs/             # Architecture, strategy, hackathon docs
```

## Quick Start

### Backend

```bash
cd backend
docker-compose up -d
# API at http://localhost:8000
# Docs at http://localhost:8000/docs
```

### Android

```bash
cd android
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug
# Open in Android Studio
```

## Key Features

- **AI-Powered Support** — Gemma 4 27B provides private, local-first family assistance
- **Agent Swarm** — 10 specialized agents handle intake, safety, logistics, relationships
- **Pregnancy Journey** — Week-by-week tracking for expecting mothers
- **Health Monitoring** — Contraction logs, kick counts, sleep tracking, caregiver load
- **Safety & Escalation** — Real-time alerts with intelligent escalation workflows
- **Resource Discovery** — Find maternal-friendly places, medical care, community resources
- **Offline-First** — Functions without internet via local Gemma 4 27B inference
- **Multi-Modal** — Android app + REST API + web dashboard

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Backend API | FastAPI (Python 3.12), async |
| Database | PostgreSQL 16, SQLAlchemy async |
| Cache | Redis 6+ |
| LLM | Gemma 4 27B (Ollama) + Gemini API fallback |
| Android | Kotlin 2.0, compileSdk 36, minSdk 29 |
| Auth | Firebase Auth + JWT |
| Deployment | Docker Compose |

## Hackathon Tracks (Gemma 4 Good)

| Prize | Implementation |
|-------|---------------|
| **Ollama** | Primary serving — Gemma 4 27B via Ollama |
| **LiteRT** | On-device Gemma inference for Android |
| **llama.cpp** | CPU-only fallback for low-resource environments |
| **Cactus** | Intelligent routing: local / cloud / rules |
| **Unsloth** | Fine-tuned Gemma 4 27B for family crisis support |
| **Future of Education** | AI learning assistant for children |
| **Digital Equity** | Offline-first, works on low-end devices |
| **Safety & Trust** | Zero-data-leaving-device, explainable AI |
| **Global Resilience** | Functions in disaster zones, multilingual |

## Documentation

- [Integration Strategy](INTEGRATION_STRATEGY.md) — Full architecture and migration plan
- [Backend Architecture](backend/ARCHITECTURE.md) — fscompanion system design
- [Android Design](android/DESIGNMASTER.md) — UI/UX design system
- [Gemma Integration Plan](backend/GEMMA_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md) — LLM deployment details

## License

MIT
", "path": "/home/azureuser/family-companion/README.md"}

{"content": """"Local LLM client — Ollama/llama.cpp wrapper for Gemma 4 27B."""

import asyncio
import json
from typing import Any, AsyncGenerator, Optional

import aiohttp

from src.config import settings


class LocalGemmaClient:
    """Client for local Gemma 4 27B inference via Ollama (OpenAI-compatible API)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
    ):
        self.base_url = base_url or settings.LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL
        self.model = model or settings.LOCAL_LLM_MODEL
        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None

    async def initialize(self):
        """Initialize HTTP session."""
        if self._session is None:
            timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=300)  # 27B takes time
            self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(
                base_url=self.base_url,
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                timeout=timeout,
            )

    async def close(self):
        """Close HTTP session."""
        if self._session:
            await self._session.close()
            self._session = None

    async def _ensure_session(self):
        if self._session is None:
            await self.initialize()

    async def health_check(self) -> bool:
        """Check if Ollama is running and the model is available."""
        await self._ensure_session()
        try:
            async with self._session.get("/api/tags") as resp:
                if resp.status != 200:
                    return False
                data = await resp.json()
                models = [m.get("name", "") for m in data.get("models", [])]
                return any(self.model in m for m in models)
        except Exception:
            return False

    async def generate(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        system_prompt: str | None = None,
        temperature: float = 0.7,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        top_p: float = 0.95,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Generate a response from local Gemma 4 27B."""
        await self._ensure_session()

        messages = []
        if system_prompt:
            messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system_prompt})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})

        payload = {
            "model": self.model,
            "messages": messages,
            "temperature": temperature,
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "top_p": top_p,
            "stream": False,
        }

        async with self._session.post(
            "/v1/chat/completions",
            json=payload,
        ) as response:
            if response.status != 200:
                text = await response.text()
                raise Exception(f"Local LLM error {response.status}: {text}")

            data = await response.json()

        choice = data.get("choices", [{}])[0]
        usage = data.get("usage", {})

        return {
            "text": choice.get("message", {}).get("content", ""),
            "model": self.model,
            "tokens_used": usage.get("total_tokens", 0),
            "prompt_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
            "completion_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens", 0),
            "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason", "unknown"),
        }

    async def stream(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        system_prompt: str | None = None,
        temperature: float = 0.7,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[str, None]:
        """Stream response from local Gemma 4 27B."""
        await self._ensure_session()

        messages = []
        if system_prompt:
            messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system_prompt})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})

        payload = {
            "model": self.model,
            "messages": messages,
            "temperature": temperature,
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "stream": True,
        }

        async with self._session.post(
            "/v1/chat/completions",
            json=payload,
        ) as response:
            if response.status != 200:
                text = await response.text()
                raise Exception(f"Local LLM stream error {response.status}: {text}")

            async for line in response.content:
                line_text = line.decode("utf-8").strip()
                if not line_text or line_text == "data: [DONE]":
                    continue
                if line_text.startswith("data: "):
                    line_text = line_text[6:]
                try:
                    chunk = json.loads(line_text)
                    delta = chunk.get("choices", [{}])[0].get("delta", {})
                    content = delta.get("content", "")
                    if content:
                        yield content
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue

    66|        """

    97|        # ── RULES route ──

   181|    async def stream(

   185|        temperature: float = 0.7,
